positions.name: Amer Sports, Inc.
positions.sector: Consumer Discretionary — Apparel, Footwear & Sporting Goods
positions.catalyst: Q2 2026 reported before the open TODAY (Aug 18): a clean beat AND a raise on every line. Revenue +32% y/y to $1,633M (+30% ex-FX); adj. EPS $0.22 vs $0.11 consensus (a 100% surprise); group operating margin +300bps ex-tariff-refunds. Every region and every segment grew double digits — Technical Apparel +32% (Arc'teryx), Outdoor Performance +37% (Salomon softgoods), Ball & Racquet +24% (Wilson Tennis 360). Full-year guidance raised across the board: Technical Apparel and Outdoor Performance revenue growth to 22-24%, Ball & Racquet to 10-12%, adj. gross margin to 59-59.5%, operating margin to 13.4-13.7%, and adj. diluted EPS to $1.18-1.23 from $1.10-1.15.
positions.driver: This is the day's cleanest under-reaction. The options market priced an 8.9% earnings move; the stock is up ~0.8% pre-market ($32.84 vs $32.57 close) on a 2x EPS beat plus a four-line guidance raise — so there is nothing to chase and the gap risk is already spent. AS sits ~23% below its $42.76 52-week high and inside the $32.02-$37.17 base it has traded since March, meaning a re-rate toward the top of that base is a 10-13% move against a defined 6% stop. It is also the right side of today's tape: QQQ is -1.2% pre-market on a semiconductor/AI unwind (SMH -3%, MU -4.9%, our own AMAT -4.5%) while the Dow is flat-to-green — a non-tech consumer compounder with a fresh, company-specific catalyst has the least correlation to that unwind. Stop $30.87 sits below every 2026 monthly low except March's $30.55, so invalidation is unambiguous.
positions.risks: The headline EPS is flattered by net tariff refunds — management explicitly frames results 'excluding the benefit from net tariff refunds' and the CFO has said the company has 'no visibility at all' into future refunds, so the quality of the beat is lower than the print suggests and the market may be discounting it for exactly that reason. AS has repeatedly failed at the top of this range in 2026 (Feb $42.76, then straight down), and Anta's controlling stake is a persistent secondary-offering overhang. Chinese-consumer and tariff exposure both cut against a discretionary apparel name, and a broad risk-off session (S&P futures -0.5%, oil up, yields up) can drown a good print. Under-reaction can also mean the market simply disagrees — a stock that does not rally on a beat-and-raise often drifts lower.
